metaTitle: Sasadu Festival of Alavanyo, Akrofu, Saviefe and Sovie
metaDescription: Sasadu is the October festival of four Volta Region towns, Sovie, Alavanyo, Saviefe and Akrofu, who share an origin at Notsie and take turns to host it. What happens and how to go.
subtitle: Four towns, one festival
answer: Sasadu is an October festival shared by four communities in the Hohoe area of the Volta Region: Sovie, Alavanyo, Saviefe and Akrofu. They trace their roots to Notsie, in present-day Togo, and the festival, hosted by each town in turn, renews the friendship between them with traditional rites and a grand durbar of chiefs.

sections.title: What Sasadu celebrates
sections.html: The name stands for the Sovie, Alavanyo, Saviefe, Akrofu Development Union, and the festival is a symbol of unity and peace between the four communities, who say they are of one stock that migrated from Notsie.[[1]] It is celebrated each October, with the towns taking turns to host, and its centre is a grand durbar of chiefs with traditional rites.[[1,2]]

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: the four towns are near Hohoe in the Volta Region, in hill country close to the Wli waterfalls.
Find the host: ask which town is hosting that year before you travel.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.

faq.a: An October festival shared by Sovie, Alavanyo, Saviefe and Akrofu in Ghana’s Volta Region, celebrating their common origin and friendship.
